identity.name: Hanthawaddy Kingdom
native_names: ဟံသာဝတီ နေပြည်တော် (Hanthawaddy Naypyidaw)
ဍုၚ် ဟံသာဝတဳ (Mon: Hongsawatoi)

land.text: Martaban province, which Gadu (Wareru) seized from Pagan in 1285 and declared a kingdom on 30 January 1287

predecessors.note: Pegu and the delta follow at an undated point (Wareru page: 'now king of three Mon-speaking regions'). Cliopatria's Pagan row ends 1293, the Pagan dossier (se-01-c) moves it to 1297.

land.text: Pegu and the delta in late 1538-1539, Martaban and the south in May 1541

successors.note: Toungoo annexed Hanthawaddy (Toungoo-Hanthawaddy War infobox). A Mon revival under Smim Sawhtut in 1550-1552, 'quickly defeated' by Bayinnaung in March 1552 (Hanthawaddy page), is not drawn.

capitals.name: Martaban (Mottama)
capitals.note: Wareru's court was at Martaban; Pegu was governed by his minister Laik-Gi; 'In 1287, he did not yet control Pegu, and his realm was technically the Martaban Kingdom'.

capitals.name: Hanthawaddy Pegu (Bago)
capitals.note: A footnote says the kingdom 'would later be known as Hanthawaddy Kingdom after the capital was moved to Hanthawaddy Pegu in 1369/70'. Takayutpi evacuated the capital in late 1538 (Toungoo-Hanthawaddy War page).

capitals.name: Martaban (Mottama), the rump
capitals.note: Saw Binnya, who 'had declared himself king of Hanthawaddy after Takayutpi's death', held Martaban until May 1541.

correction.text: the Martaban province (Mon State and Kayin State), Wareru's kingdom in 1287

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1287-1295. Gadu 'declared himself king of Martaban' on 30 January 1287 (crowned c. 5 April 1287); 'In 1287, he did not yet control Pegu, and his realm was technically the Martaban Kingdom'. Cliopatria starts in 1294 with the three regions; Pegu and the delta (Tarabya's) join c. 1296 ('emerged as the sole ruler of three Mon-speaking provinces of Bassein, Pegu and Martaban c. 1296'); years corrected by the se-01-d reviewer.

Years only: 1296-1362 (from Wareru becoming sole ruler of the three provinces c. 1296). 78,823 km2 (249 cells): the three Mon-speaking regions of Lower Burma, Martaban, Pegu and the Irrawaddy delta (Mon, Kayin, Bago, Yangon, Ayeyarwady in the gazetteer; 248 of the 249 cells lie in Cliopatria's Pagan shape of 1293). The Wareru page does not carry Wareru south of Martaban: 'he did not control other former Pagan territories farther south' (Tavoy, Mergui, Tenasserim). No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: the 1294 shape without the Martaban province (Mon and Kayin), 'in open rebellion from 1363 to 1388'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1363-1388: 'Mottama was in open rebellion from 1363 to 1388'. The Forty Years' War page has Razadarit 'reunified his provinces', taking Donwun by late 1388. The Martaban province is taken out of Pegu's shape for the years of the rebellion; the rebel side has no dossier.

Years only: 1389-1428 (the shape stands, 78,768 km2, three cells fewer than 1294). Razadarit reunified the provinces by late 1388; the Forty Years' War (1385-1424) left 'no long-term changes' (infobox). Ava's gains in Arakan 1404-1406 and the delta in 1415 were short.
78,317 km2: three cells more than 1375; no event on the pages opened (Dhammazedi page: reign 1471-1492 with 'no campaigns'; the 1420s-1530s are the 'golden age').
78,372 km2: the same outline within one cell; no event on the pages opened. Unverified: page budget.
78,206 km2: coastline vertices change (58 to 88) with the same area; Dhammazedi (1471-1492) died in 1492; no event on the pages opened. Unverified: page budget.
78,179 km2: one cell fewer; no event on the pages opened. Unverified: page budget.

Years only: 1512-1537. 78,206 km2, the outline the war found in 1534-35. Toungoo 'took Pegu without firing a shot' in late 1538 and held 'two out of the three Hanthawaddy provinces (the Irrawaddy delta and Pegu)' by 1539; the next two keyframes carry it.

minus.text: Pegu, evacuated by Takayutpi in late 1538

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1538 only: 'Toungoo forces took Pegu without firing a shot' in late 1538 (the Hanthawaddy page says 'Taungoo captured Bago and the Irrawaddy Delta in 1538-39'; this page puts Pegu in late 1538, not 1539). Pegu province is read as Bago and Yangon; the delta (Ayeyarwady) is still Hanthawaddy's until the Naungyo defeat in 1538-39.

Years only: 1539-1541. 29,794 km2 (99 cells: Mon and Kayin): the Martaban rump. 'Toungoo then held two out of the three Hanthawaddy provinces (the Irrawaddy delta and Pegu), with Martaban still independent'; Martaban was attacked in November 1540 and fell in May 1541, after which Moulmein and the south submitted. Cliopatria draws the rump to 1546; the Hanthawaddy page's revival of 1550-1552 is not drawn (its extent is not on the page).

ledger.note: 30 January 1287: Gadu (Wareru) declares himself king of Martaban. 'On 30 January 1287, Gadu declared himself king of Martaban'; crowned c. 5 April 1287; he had seized Martaban after the assassination of Governor Aleimma (c. 11 January 1285). 'The declaration did not elicit any action by Pagan, which was amidst its death throes.' The page names Martaban, not a boundary.

c. 1296: Wareru defeats his ally and rival Tarabya, 'the self-proclaimed king of Pegu (Bago)', who 'had gained control of both Pegu and Dala', and 'emerged as the sole ruler of three Mon-speaking provinces of Bassein, Pegu and Martaban c. 1296' (Wareru page; 'By late 1296, the relationship had deteriorated to the point of war'). In 1287 'he did not yet control Pegu'. Year and counterpart corrected by the se-01-d reviewer (was 1294, Cliopatria's shape year, from pagan-kingdom).
1363: Mottama rises against Pegu. 'Mottama was in open rebellion from 1363 to 1388.' Hatched as rebel land; the rebels have no dossier.
1369/70: the court moves from Martaban to Hanthawaddy Pegu. A footnote says the kingdom 'would later be known as Hanthawaddy Kingdom after the capital was moved to Hanthawaddy Pegu in 1369/70'.

region.text: the approaches to Pegu (Hmawbi, Dagon, Pankyaw)

ledger.note: December 1385: Ava invades Lower Burma. The war 'began c. December 1385'; 'Ava had a clear path to Pegu' after a victory at Hmawbi, Tarabya took Pankyaw and Razadarit cut off and retook it. Truce 1391-1401.
1388: Razadarit reunifies his provinces. 'Razadarit "reunified his provinces," taking Donwun by late 1388'; the Hanthawaddy page ends Mottama's rebellion in 1388.
1391: the first phase of the war ends in a truce. The page: the war was fought 'during two separate periods: 1385 to 1391, and 1401 to 1424', with truces in 1391-1401 and 1403-1408.

region.text: Pegu and the border with Ava

ledger.note: 1401: Pegu invades Upper Burma in force and the war resumes. 'Pegu invades Upper Burma in force' (1401); Hanthawaddy briefly held Gu Htut, a border town within Ava; Ava took Kale, Mohnyin and Launggyet in 1404-1406 and Pegu dislodged Avan troops from Arakan in 1408.

region.text: Arakan (Launggyet), the western kingdom of Rakhine

ledger.note: 1412: Arakan becomes a tributary of Pegu. The infobox gives 'Arakan tributary of Pegu (1412-1421)'; the Hanthawaddy page gives 1413 to 1421 ('making the western kingdom of Rakhine a tributary from 1413 to 1421').
1415: Minye Kyawswa of Ava conquers the Irrawaddy delta. 'Minye Kyawswa invades Hanthawaddy (1414-1415), conquers the Irrawaddy delta in 1415, and forces Razadarit to flee to Martaban.' Hatched.
March 1415: Minye Kyawswa is killed and Pegu 'reconquered' the delta in 1415.
1421: the tribute of Arakan ends with Razadarit's death. Infobox 'tributary of Pegu (1412-1421)'; 'Minkhaung I and Razadarit die' in 1421-1422.

region.text: Pegu and the border with Ava

ledger.note: Early 1424: the war ends in stalemate. Binnya Ran I made peace by giving his sister Shin Sawbu to Thihathu and Ava withdrew; 'ended in a stalemate, preserving the independence of Hanthawaddy' (infobox 'No long-term changes').
Late 1538: Toungoo takes Pegu. 'Toungoo forces took Pegu without firing a shot'; Takayutpi evacuated the capital.

1538-39: the Irrawaddy delta falls. Bayinnaung beat the retreating Hanthawaddy army at Naungyo, in the delta, after which Toungoo 'held two out of the three Hanthawaddy provinces (the Irrawaddy delta and Pegu)'; the Hanthawaddy page: 'Taungoo captured Bago and the Irrawaddy Delta in 1538-39'. The page gives no date for the battle.
November 1540: Toungoo attacks Martaban. 'In November 1540, a 13,000-strong Toungoo force attacked Martaban.'
May 1541: Martaban falls. After about seven months, 'in May 1541, Smim Payu's second naval attack broke the harbor defenses'.
May 1541: Toungoo annexes Martaban, Moulmein and the south. 'After Martaban's fall, the governors of Moulmein and the southern territories (present-day Mon State) submitted.'

May 1541: the last Hanthawaddy king falls at Martaban and Toungoo annexes the Mon kingdom (infobox 'Toungoo annexed Hanthawaddy'). The Hanthawaddy page's 'from 1550 to 1552' covers a brief revival that Bayinnaung 'quickly defeated ... in March 1552'.

wars.name: Mottama rebellion
wars.outcome: 'Mottama was in open rebellion from 1363 to 1388'; Razadarit 'reunified his provinces', taking Donwun by late 1388.
wars.note: The page says nothing else about the rebels. The Forty Years' War page adds Razadarit's retaking of Donwun and his Bassein-Myaungmya campaign of late 1389.

wars.name: Forty Years' War
wars.outcome: Stalemate: 'preserving the independence of Hanthawaddy'; Ava held Kale, Mohnyin and Launggyet from 1404-1406 and the delta briefly in 1415; Arakan was a Pegu tributary 1412-1421.
wars.note: Two periods, 1385-1391 and 1401-1424, with truces 1391-1401 and 1403-1408. The lead says 1385-1423.

wars.name: Toungoo-Hanthawaddy War
wars.outcome: Toungoo took Pegu in late 1538, the delta in 1538-39 and Martaban in May 1541 and annexed Hanthawaddy.
wars.note: Infobox c. November 1534 to May 1541; the chronicles begin the war in 896 ME (30 March 1534 to 29 March 1535). Prome and the Confederation of Shan States were Toungoo's allies.

certainty.note: The Mon heartland (Martaban, Pegu, the delta) is a coherent outline, but no page gives a frontier; the Tenasserim and Tavoy side, and the Prome and Toungoo frontier, are approximate.

sources.title: Hanthawaddy Kingdom
sources.note: Infobox 1287-1552, the three regions, Forty Years' War, Toungoo conquest; no area, no capital years.

notes:
Start moved from Cliopatria's 1294 to 30 January 1287 (Wareru page), end moved from its 1546 to May 1541 (Toungoo-Hanthawaddy War page); Cliopatria draws the Martaban rump to 1546. The Hanthawaddy infobox gives 1287-1552 and its text '1287 to 1539 and from 1550 to 1552'; the 1550-1552 revival (a rebel state under a Mon claimant, 'quickly defeated' in March 1552) is not drawn because the pages opened give no extent, and it has no dossier: a candidate for the additions batch (rebel).
Page budget (5 pages) spent. No page gives an area, so the infobox comparison was impossible. Unverified: the 1429, 1450, 1487 and 1507 shapes (differences of 1-3 cells, no events).
Page conflicts: Pegu fell in late 1538 (Toungoo-Hanthawaddy War page, 'not 1539') while the Hanthawaddy page gives 1538-39; Arakan's tribute 1412-1421 (Forty Years' War infobox) against 1413-1421 (Hanthawaddy page); the Forty Years' War lead says 1385-1423 and its body 1424; Hanthawaddy 'became formally independent of Sukhothai in 1330' (Hanthawaddy page) against Martaban's breakaway in 1319 (Sukhothai page, used in the sukhothai-kingdom ledger); the Hanthawaddy page does not mention Tenasserim and the Wareru page excludes it, while the Sukhothai ledger (Cliopatria's 1294 shape) draws it in Sukhothai's sphere.
Overlap to reconcile: the pagan-kingdom dossier (se-01-c) records the loss of all Lower Burma ('Thaton and Lower Burma') to Hanthawaddy on 30 January 1287, while the Wareru page says Wareru held only Martaban in 1287 and 'did not yet control Pegu'; this ledger gives Martaban in 1287 and bridges Pegu and the delta to 1294 (confidence 1).
Suzerainty is carried by the suzerains: Sukhothai (nominal vassal from 1287 to 1330 or 1319; the sukhothai-kingdom ledger has the tint), the Yuan (recognition in 1298; yuan-dynasty), Ava (the 1415 occupation is in both ledgers) and Toungoo. Counterpart without a dossier: the Mottama rebels (1363-1388), slug mottama-rebels in the ledger, a rebel candidate; Arakan before 1429 (Launggyet).
Gazetteer cell checks (not pages): the 1294 shape is Mon 25, Kayin 65, Bago 32, Yangon 33, Ayeyarwady 83 cells; the 1540 shape is Mon and Kayin only (99 cells) and the 150 cells it loses are 147 inside First Toungoo's 1540 shape.
